work_packages.name: On the CPU alone, a spring's water runs down a valley, fills a pool to its sill, quickens through a narrows and reaches a lake, and the solved flow is a chart the water map takes
work_packages.quality_bar: A steady river a hydraulics text would accept, held to closed forms as SWASHES' reference cases hold a flood code: discharge kept, pools level, a jump where momentum puts it. Nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: `thrum-river-model` takes a bed grid, declared sources, the bodies water may reach and Manning's `n`, and gives the steady depth and current in every cell. On a valley the test makes, with a spring, a pool behind a sill, a narrows and a basin at its foot: discharge through every cross-section is within 1% of the spring's; away from where the stream enters it the pool's level is flat within 3 cm, and it stands between 1.3 and 1.9 critical depths over its sill; the speed in the narrows over the speed above it is at least the ratio of the wet widths less a fifth; a hollow beside the channel, lower than the water and cut off from it by ground, stays dry.
items.ask: Read the test. Are the expected figures worked out there from continuity and the weir relation, without the solver? Would a solver that routes water down the steepest slope and takes its depth from Manning cell by cell fail the pool?

items.statement: In section the solver meets closed forms the tests work out. Water at rest over a rough bed with dry ground stays at rest to 1e-12 m. A steady flow over a bump has its hydraulic jump within two cells of the closed form's place and a mean depth error under 3% of the critical depth at 0.25 m cells, smaller at 0.125 m. Over a bed made for a known depth with friction, a slow flow is within 1% in depth, and a fast one within 8% at 0.25 m cells and under two thirds of that error at 0.125 m. A sheet on a slope of 0.3 whose bed falls three times its depth across a cell stands within 8% of Manning's normal depth.
items.ask: Are the closed forms in the test its own arithmetic (Bernoulli's branches and the jump condition, a bed integrated for a chosen depth, Manning's normal depth), as in part 1 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py`? Would Audusse's reconstruction, 23% over on the steep sheet there, fail it?

items.statement: Depth is never negative and no value is ever not a number, over 200 seeded beds with dry patches, steps and sources. Below a spring, over ground the start leaves dry, the water wets its way down to the mouth. A solve is refused, by name and place, when water reaches its rectangle's edge, when a source has no way down to a declared body, and when a source body's level anywhere in its range lies below the outlet's sill. Each stretch of channel narrower than four cells is reported by place.

The solve keeps an energy account. The head lost cell by cell, times discharge, sums to the discharge times the head between the source and the mouth within 2%. The chart's loss is the power that breaks the surface, as the design defines it: head lost beyond bed friction, and friction's power beyond the chop's cap. In the section of part 2 the loss at the ledge is at least five times the chute's and fifty times the glide's, and the pool's is under 2% of the ledge's. In the valley of WP1.1 at least 60% of the head lost beyond friction lies round its rock and below its narrows and ledge, in under 40% of the wet cells. A straight uniform channel has none: under 1% of its friction power.
items.ask: Does the test compute friction's power from Manning's relation itself and compare, or does it read both sides from the solver's own account?

items.statement: A solve stops when the level's rate and the imbalance of discharge between sections are under the profile's tolerances, and reports its steps, cell updates, seconds and residual. One that does not get there inside its step budget is refused by name and writes nothing. It works on wet cells and their neighbours: doubling the rectangle round the same valley changes its cell updates by under 5%. Two solves of one input give the same bytes, on one thread and on eight.

The solve writes each reach as a chart `thrum-water-model` declares: level over the whole footprint, lying under the bed in every cell the solve left dry, current, loss, footprint, ends and join lengths. The stored chart's level and current at every wet cell's centre are the solver's, and the chart's wet cells, where its level is over the bed inside its footprint, are exactly the solver's: on the WP1.1 valley the hollow cut off by ground is dry in the chart and in the map. With a basin at its mouth and a spring at its head, `thrum-water-model` prepares it with no refusal. The map's level and current are the stored chart's wherever the join's weight is nothing. Inside the mouth's join they are `WATERS`' mix of the chart's row and the basin's at that cell's weight, backwater included, with the basin's stage at both ends of its range; the row meets the basin's across the mouth with no step; and the waterline is where the level meets the bed.
items.ask: Is the chart declared only through `thrum-water-model`'s public interface, with no change to that crate in this work package? Does the test work the expected joined row out from the join's documented weight and the two rows, with no joined cell skipped? Would a chart that gave a dry cell the nearest wet level fail the hollow?

items.statement: A river file holds a solve's output and decodes to the same bytes. Its key is a hash of the bed inside the rectangle, the declaration, the profile and the solver's version; changing a bed cell, a discharge, `n` or the version changes the key, and a file whose key does not match is refused by name. The reader is in `thrum-water-model`, which gains no dependency on the solver.

`scripts/river_cost.py` records a solve of the WP1.1 valley at 0.25 m cells on this Mac: wet cells, steps, cell updates and seconds, with the commit, the load on the machine and a release build. `check` fails only when the solve cannot be measured or the committed record lacks one of those. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Was the record taken on this work package's solver, in a release build, and does it say how its cell updates compare with part 5's count?

work_packages.name: On the CPU alone, where the ground drops away the stream leaves it as a waterfall: its path, speed and thickness are worked out, and its water lands in the pool below and runs on
work_packages.quality_bar: A fall whose every number follows from the flow at its lip and the height it drops, as a hydraulics text gives a free overfall: nothing placed or tuned by hand, and no water made or lost between the lip and the pool.

items.statement: Brinks are found from the bed alone: runs of faces where the ground, followed downhill, drops at least the profile's least fall (0.75 m) at a slope steeper than the profile's steepest chart slope (1.5). On beds the test makes, a 3 m cliff is a brink along its whole lip; a 0.4 m ledge and a slope of 1 are not, and stay in the chart. The brinks are the same at every discharge.

Water leaves a brink freely and enters the solve again where its path lands. The discharge of the reach below a fall is within 1% of the reach above. The last cell above a lip stands between 0.95 and 1.25 of the critical depth where the flow above is slow, and within 10% of the flow's own depth where it is fast; the fall's launch depth is 0.715 of the critical depth in the first case and the flow's own in the second. The river is cut into reaches at its falls, and the cliff's face is in no chart. A path that lands in a declared basin ends there; one that lands on ground gentler than the steepest chart slope starts a reach there.
items.ask: Does the test show a lower dry cell in place of the lip's face failing the lip's depth, as part 4 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py` does?

items.statement: Ruling 1 is built: a chart may declare a brink end, where the ground drops away below its level. `thrum-water-model` prepares such a chart, gives its own row up to the brink with no mix, and names no body on the ground below; the same chart without the end declared is refused as before. A chart below a fall has no source body. Every existing test of `thrum-water-model` passes unchanged.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test brink_end && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Is the change to the map's preparation confined to a declared brink end, so that no chart an existing test or the example declares is prepared differently? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` edited?

items.statement: A fall record gives, for each place along the lip, the water's path with the time it takes, its discharge for each metre of lip and its launch speed, with stable IDs for its segments. The f64 reference in `thrum-water-model` gives at any point of the path the speed, `sqrt(v0^2 + 2 g z)`; the thickness, discharge over speed; the white share, 0 at the lip and 1 at `6 q^0.32` m of path; and the presence, thickness over the tear thickness and at most 1. Clear of the rock the path is the free path within 1% in throw; where the rock stands in its way it follows the rock's face and never passes through the bed.
items.ask: Are the expected paths, speeds and thicknesses the closed forms of part 4 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py`, worked out in the test?

items.statement: For a body below at any level in its stage's range, the plunge is where each path meets that level, and it moves as the level moves. Each segment's births follow the fall's power, `rho g q z` for each metre of lip, split between foam and submerged air by the profile's share. Each segment's impulse a tick is the wave share times its momentum flux into the surface times the sheet's pattern arriving there, with its mean over the pattern's loop removed: over that loop its mean is under 1% of its rms, its rms is the design's figure within 5%, and the same tick gives the same impulse on every run. A path that lands on bare ground gives no births and no impulses.
`thrum-water-model` still builds with no graphics device and no dependency on the solver, and neither crate's new files or tests hold a place, a preset or a water type that belongs to a game.

work_packages.name: On the CPU alone, the river answers its source: it runs deeper, wider and faster as its lake rises, rough in its riffles and smooth in its pools, in a calm as in a gale
work_packages.quality_bar: A river whose state follows its lake as a rating curve does, and whose roughness follows its bed as a riffle and a pool do in Red Dead Redemption 2: read between solved flows by the same function a GPU and a game are held to.

items.statement: A river with a source body is solved at levels across that body's stage range no more than 0.3 m apart, and a spring-fed one at the discharges declared. Each sample records its gauge level, and the river reports the range of its gauge. Below a basin with a sill the discharge rises with the level at every sample, and between the lowest and highest sample it grows as the head over the sill to a power between 1.3 and 2.

Ruling 2's mix is built: in `thrum-water-model` a chart's row is the mix, linear in the gauge, of the two samples that bracket it; the gauge is the source body's level where the river has one and the river's stage where it has none; and every chart of a river takes the same gauge. In cells both samples wet, between samples 0.3 m apart the mixed row is within 1 cm in depth and 25% in speed of a solve at that level. As the gauge moves 1 cm the waterline on a bank of 1 in 10 or steeper moves by at most one cell. A chart with one sample answers to the bit as before, and its stage adds to its level. Every existing test of `thrum-water-model` passes unchanged.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test gauge && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Does the test compare the mixed row with a fresh solve at the level between, in the cells both samples wet, as part 3 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/river_proof.py` does, and would a chart left at one sample with its level raised fail it? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` edited?

items.statement: A fall follows the gauge. Where both samples run a part of the lip, its record's discharge, launch speed and path are the mix of its samples', so the sheet's thickness and the plunge's power and impulses grow with the river. A part only the upper sample runs gives no sheet, no births and no impulses below its lip cell's wetting gauge, and from there its discharge and launch depth rise from nothing, with no step, to the upper sample's. At every gauge tried no running part of a fall lands on a dry cell of a reach, and a reach fed only by that fall is dry while its lip is dry.

Between two samples a cell holds water only from its wetting gauge, and wetting spreads from the lower sample's water and from where an inflow enters. In valleys the test makes and the solver solves: a hollow behind a ridge that only the upper sample overtops is dry, with the ridge, at the lower sample and at every gauge below the ridge's wetting, and fills from its bed once the ridge's lowest point is wet. A reach below a fall whose lip only the upper sample runs, with no wet cell in the lower sample, is dry at the lower sample and at every gauge below the lip's wetting; above it the reach is wet from its landing to its lower end, its depth and current rise from nothing with no step, and at the upper sample its row is the upper sample's. At every gauge tried no wet cell is cut off from both the lower sample's water and a running inflow, and a dry cell has no wave support and no shore margin.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test wetting && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Are the wet cells judged at gauges either side of each wetting, the ridge's and the lip's, as parts 8 and 10 of `docs/evidence/RIVERS/design-proof/` do? Would a dry cell at the nearest wet level fail the hollow, and a flood seeded only from the lower sample's wet cells fail the dry reach?

items.statement: The flow's chop is written as two flow gains in each sample. Its rms height is `c d min(S, S_cap)` from the depth and the friction slope: none at rest; in the valley of WP1.1 at least 20 times larger in the riffle than in the pool; never more than 0.15 of the depth. It is all in the short band at 0.15 m of depth and all in the long band at 1 m.
items.ask: Does the test work the expected heights out from Manning's relation at the solver's depths and speeds, with its own arithmetic?

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the CPU: `thrum-water-model` holds the two flow bands' spectrum and an f64 evaluator on the cascades' loop, and its surface model adds them at a chart's flow gains through the same sum, depth limit and moments as a cascade. With no wind, the model's surface over a riffle has the chop's rms height within 10%, and over a sea and a basin it is the level. With the bands not named in the profile every answer of the model is what it was to the bit.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test flow_bands && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model

items.statement: Ruling 6 is built: `examples/water` has a river selection, off by default. With it off the island's ground, bodies and tick page are what they were and the hand-made channel is as `WATERS` built it. With it on the island has a valley above the lake with a spring, a riffle, a pool behind a sill, a narrows with rocks and a cliff of about 4 m over a plunge pool, and both its rivers are declared and solved. The game loads each river file by its key; a native game with none solves and writes it and says so, and its next preparation solves nothing.

items.statement: `WATERS`' own channel tests pass unchanged with the selection off.

Ruling 2 is built on the GPU, in the map and in what is drawn from it. The map: with the gauge at a sample, between two and at each end of its range, the body, depth and current the GPU's map gives inside each river are `thrum-water-model`'s at the tolerance `WATERS` WP4.1's test states. In a scene the test declares, which has a hollow behind a ridge that only the upper sample overtops and a reach below a fall that the lower sample leaves wholly dry, the cells the GPU map finds wet are `thrum-water-model`'s at gauges either side of each wetting: the hollow is dry until the ridge is wet, and the reach is dry at the lower sample and until its lip runs and from there is wet along its length, each with its depth inside that tolerance at both samples and between them. The draw: the water is drawn where the map has it, and the depth it writes is the surface a game is answered. Two cameras read that depth, each where the ray through the middle of its frame meets the water: one looking down from 2 m straight above a place, and one on the bank, 2 m above the water and 6 m from the place it is aimed at, looking across and downstream with a 55° field of view. In that scene, at those gauges either side of each wetting, at the hollow's middle and at places no more than 2 m apart along the reach, read from above, the water writes nothing above the ground while the map has the place dry, and once the map has it wet the depth the water writes there is within 0.010 m of `thrum-water-model`'s surface at the same place and display time. On the island, with the gauge at a sample, between two and at each end of its range, in a trade wind, at places no more than 2 m apart along the whole wet length of both rivers, off the mesh's vertices, in one frame at each place: from above, the depth the water writes is within 0.010 m of `thrum-water-model`'s surface with the swell alone running, and of the body query's answer with the wind's waves running too, at the same place and display time; from the bank, with the wind's waves running, it is within the greater of 0.010 m and 4 pixels of the body query's answer, where 4 pixels is the height the surface would have to rise or fall by to move 4 pixels in a 2560×1440 frame from that camera. The same two bounds hold in every frame of the scene's first 7 s at the lake's lowest stage, with the wind's waves running, at the two places in the tidal reach where reviews found a miss: from above at (337.83, 5.23) and from the bank at (340.71, 5.80). No other camera, place or time decides the depth drawn inside a river. The look: a float sits at the drawn surface, with no air under it and no stretch where it hangs sunk below the water around it, and no seam, gap or step shows along either river or across any of the three ends, from above and from the bank alike. The joins: at each end's edge (the lake's outlet, the stream's mouth in the lake, the river's mouth in the sea) there is no step: with the lake's stage and the tide each at both ends of its range and the swell running, the depths the water writes either side of the edge differ by what `thrum-water-model`'s surface differs by between those two places, to the tolerance `WATERS` WP4.1's test states. Guard: `river_gpu`, on the device because only a device draws the water and writes its depth.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at 2560×1440 and `realtime` sequences in a trade wind with its swell running: the stream's float in the pool, the river's float halfway down the river and in the tidal reach, and the water across each of the three ends, each from above (about 6 m over the water, looking down at about 45°) and from the bank (2 m above the water, about 6 m away). 1. Each float sits at the drawn surface: no air shows under it, and it does not hang sunk below the water around it. 2. The water's line on each float rises and falls with the waves that pass it, and does not jump from one frame to the next. 3. Along each river and across each of the three ends, neither camera shows a seam, a gap or a step in the surface.

work_packages.name: On a windless day the stream still reads as running water: its riffles are rough and glitter, its pools lie glassy, and foam forms below its ledges and behind its rocks and trails away downstream
work_packages.quality_bar: Running water as in Red Dead Redemption 2: fast shallows that are rough and bright, slow pools that mirror, detail that travels at the water's own speed and faster in the narrows, and foam in streaks from every rock and ledge, with no sliding sheet, pulse or stamped pattern.

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the GPU. With the wind at nothing, the drawn surface over the riffle carries chop; over the pool its rms height is under a tenth of the riffle's; on the lake and the sea it is flat. A scene whose profile does not name the flow bands compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before this work package.
items.ask: Is the comparison of shader text, passes and storage made against the commit before this work package?

items.statement: The flow bands are carried by the current. Tracked across submitted frames in a calm where the current is 0.5 m/s and 1.5 m/s, the detail's mean speed downstream is within a fifth of the current; in the pool's still corner it does not drift.

The game's query answers the flow bands. With the wind at nothing, points posted through the query over the riffle, at a footprint that reads each band's finest level, come back with the height, slope and rate of change of the chop drawn there: `thrum-water-model`'s two flow bands (WP3.5) at the chart's gains, read in the current and brought to each point's use tick as the query reads and brings a cascade, within the tolerance `WATERS` WP5.1's test states for a cascade, taken as that share of each band's rms height. So the answers' rms height over the riffle is the model's chop within a tenth, and over the pool it is under a tenth of the riffle's.
items.ask: Does the test post its points through the game's query and read the answers from its mailbox? Would it fail if the query's sum left out either flow band, and if a band were read at the frame's time and not brought to the use tick?

items.statement: Ruling 4 is built for a chart's loss. Foam is born below the ledge, behind the rocks and down the chute, at a rate that follows the chart's loss, and is carried downstream. With the loss births switched off the foam ages out and none is born. The glide and the pool gain no foam but what the current brings. Lowering the gauge to its lowest sample lowers the cover below the ledge. The record gives the cover each station of the valley reaches and the birth constant used.
items.ask: Is the birth constant the shallows' own, or a recorded constant of the water type with its reason in the log?

items.statement: In a dead calm the stream reads as running water: the riffle and the narrows are rough and glitter, the pool lies glassy and mirrors its banks, ripples travel downstream and faster through the narrows, and the water piled in front of a rock stays put while ripples pass over it. There is no sheet sliding at one speed, no pulse at the carriage's period, and no look of a small sea.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences in a dead calm from the bank at 2 m, across and along the riffle, the pool and the narrows, and one from 40 m above the stream, at noon and with the Sun at 15°; the same views in a trade wind.

items.statement: Foam reads as made by the flow: white below the ledge and behind each rock, drawn out into streaks that thin, break into lace and vanish downstream, gathering in the pool's slack water; none on the glide or the pool but what drifts in; no stamped or tiled pattern.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences from the bank at 2 m of the ledge, a rock in the narrows and the pool below them, and one from 40 m above, in a calm; then the same rock's reach after the gauge is taken to its lowest and highest.

items.statement: The flow bands' cadence is a named runtime value in `EFFECT-GRAPH`'s list with a declared invalidation, and neither it nor the camera changes a query answer. Over a scripted run of tick frames and repeat frames, with WP5.10's points posted over the windless riffle every tick, the answers the mailbox returns for each use tick are the same to the bit with the bands evaluated every frame and at their lowest cadence, and with the camera at the riffle and with every river outside every view's reach. At the lowest cadence the bands' producer reports not run on every frame the cadence skips, except a frame that answers a point posted over a river.
items.ask: Does the test read the answers from the game's mailbox, in the scene where WP5.10 holds them to the model, so that equality carries WP5.10's proof to every cadence and camera? Would it fail if a frame the cadence skips answered from the field last written, and if the bands stopped when the river left the view? Does it show the producer skipped at the lowest cadence, so the equality does not come from running every frame?

items.statement: In Chrome, in a calm, the riffle is rough, the pool is flat and foam trails from the ledge.

With the flow bands and the river's foam in view the paired cost record is taken again at 2560×1440, beside WP4's. Each tripwire it trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.

work_packages.name: A waterfall pours over its lip in a smooth tongue, breaks into white strands as it gathers speed and plunges into its pool, which boils, foams and sends out rings
work_packages.quality_bar: A waterfall as in Horizon Forbidden West, without its mist: falling water that speeds up and stretches as it drops, glassy at the lip and white below, a trickle as a few strands and a middling flow as a fuller fall of them, and a pool that answers it with foam, pale water and rings. The lip is glassy at every gauge. Below the lip, the heavy fall at the highest gauge is WP11's.

items.statement: Ruling 7's sheet is built. Each fall is drawn along its record's paths from the lip to the level of the body below, with the gauge at each end of its range and the pool's stage at each end of its own, and the depth it writes lies along those paths. The sheet never shows through the rock it falls past. A scene whose profile does not name falls compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before this work package.
items.ask: Is the sheet's pass before the water's gather, so that the pool's surface reads it as it reads the land?

items.statement: The sheet writes the frame contract. Tracked across submitted frames, its streaks move down the fall, faster at the foot than at the lip. Its motion output is that movement, from unjittered positions. It writes depth where its presence passes one half and reactive coverage where it is white. A pause holds it, and a capture shows it at the capture's time.

Ruling 4 is built for a plunge. With the interaction windows on the plunge pool, foam and submerged air are born along the plunge line and carried downstream, and rings leave it. With the gauge at a sample that leaves the lip dry there are no births and no rings. Every existing interaction test of `WATERS` passes unchanged.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --test plunge_gpu && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water --test interaction_gpu
items.ask: Do the rings and births stop when the lip is dry, and not merely fade?

items.statement: At its lowest and middle gauges the fall reads as falling water. At the lip it is a smooth tongue that shows the rock behind it, at the lowest, the middle and the highest gauge; it whitens down its length and breaks into strands that stretch as they gather speed, with gaps where it is thin; at the lowest gauge it is a few strands and at the middle gauge a fuller fall of them. No pattern slides at one speed, nothing tiles or repeats, and it does not read as a card. Below the lip at the highest gauge the fall draws, and its look there is WP11's and decides nothing here.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the fall from 2 m and 5 m in front, from beside it, from behind it and from 60 m and 200 m off, at the gauge's lowest and middle, at noon, with stills cropped at native size of the lip, the middle and the foot; and one `realtime` sequence from 2 m in front at the gauge's highest, at noon, with a still of the lip cropped at native size. 1. At the lip the water is a smooth tongue and the rock behind shows through it, at the lowest, the middle and the highest gauge. 2. Down its length the fall whitens and breaks into strands, with gaps where it is thin. 3. Followed through a sequence, a streak stretches and moves faster near the foot than near the lip, and no pattern slides at one speed. 4. At the lowest gauge the fall is a few strands; at the middle gauge it is fuller, and still strands with gaps. 5. Nothing tiles or repeats across the fall, and from no view does it read as a card. Points 2 to 5 are judged at the lowest and middle gauges. At the highest gauge only the lip is judged, by point 1: a curtain below it, or strands that end hard, is WP11's cue.

items.statement: The pool answers the fall: a white boil at the foot, pale water spreading from it, foam drawn off downstream in streaks, and rings that cross the pool and die at its banks. The fall on screen shows in the pool's calmer water. The pool lies against the rock at the foot of the cliff, behind the falling water and to each side of it, with a waterline like any bank's, whether the fall runs or the lip is dry. At the middle gauge there is no hard line where the sheet meets the pool. How the falling water ends at the pool at the highest gauge is WP11's and decides nothing here.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the plunge pool from its bank at 2 m, looking along the foot of the cliff, and from 15 m above, with the interaction windows on the pool, at the gauge's middle and highest; one as the gauge falls to a dry lip and the pool calms. 1. A white boil stands at the foot of the fall and pale water spreads from it. 2. Foam is drawn off downstream in streaks. 3. Rings leave the foot, cross the pool and die at its banks. 4. The fall on screen shows in the pool's calmer water. 5. The pool lies against the rock at the foot of the cliff, behind the falling water and to each side of it, with a waterline like any bank's. 6. As the gauge falls to a dry lip the pool calms and keeps that waterline. 7. At the middle gauge no hard line shows where the sheet meets the pool. At the highest gauge judge points 1 to 5 only: the ends of the falling water there, and any line they draw above or through the boil, are WP11.3's cue and do not decide this item.

items.statement: The sheet's spacing along its path is a named runtime value in `EFFECT-GRAPH`'s list with a declared invalidation, and changing it changes no query answer, birth or impulse.
In Chrome the fall draws from lip to pool, its streaks move faster at the foot than at the lip, and the pool below it foams.

With the fall filling a third of the view the paired cost record is taken again at 2560×1440, beside WP5's. Each tripwire it trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.

Ruling 5 is built: the interaction step has a current ladder, and a ring travels with the water under it. In a window that holds a pool at 0.2 m/s and a riffle at 1.5 m/s in one wet region, a stone is dropped in the pool while a source runs in the riffle. After 5 s each ring set's centre is within 0.5 m, two cells of the window, of where its own water's current carries it, in steps of 1 and of 8 ticks, and the pool's centre moves by under 0.1 m when the riffle's source is five times stronger. A ring raised on water the step carries as a blend, at a current that is no carriage current, survives the blend, on a straight stretch between two carriage currents and on a bend between three: after 5 s in steps of 1 tick it has at least half the energy of the same ring raised there with the scene's currents set to nothing, it never gains energy, and its centre has moved downstream with that water, within 0.5 m of it on the straight stretch.
items.ask: Are both ring sets raised at once in one region, and does the test show one mean current, plain or weighted, failing both centres there? Is the surviving ring raised where the step's own weights are split between carriage currents, on the straight stretch and on the bend, and would a step that damps blended cells to nothing fail it?

items.statement: The current ladder stays inside the step's count of solves and changes nothing where one current serves. Where a level's solves would pass the profile's count the step drops carriage currents before it rests a region, and reports what it dropped. On still water and on a uniform current the step's output is what it was, to the bit, and every existing interaction test of `WATERS` passes unchanged.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --test current_ladder_gpu && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water --test interaction_gpu

items.statement: Below a fall the map gives the receiving body its water and its shore margin on the rock, and no body above them, and preparation refuses a fall that the receiving water can drown. The map's answers: the test prepares four maps, each with a fall whose receiving water stands above the foot of the rock: the receiver is a basin in two and the reach below in two, under a rock one bed cell wide and under a rock four cells wide. At points a quarter of a cell apart from the lip to the foot, at each end of the receiving water's range of level in that map, `thrum-water-model` answers the upper reach on the lip, with its own row and no mix, and below the lip by the bed's height against the level the receiving body has at the foot: no body where the bed stands more than the profile's margin height above that level; the receiving body, on its shore margin as `WATERS` WP1.13 names one, where the bed stands above that level by no more than the margin height; and the receiving body where the bed lies below that level. Wherever the receiving body is named its depth is that level less the bed, so it runs from negative on the margin through nothing at the waterline to the foot's with no step. Both maps with the wide rock hold points of all three kinds. The GPU's map gives the same body and depth at those points, at the tolerance `WATERS` WP4.1's test states. The refusal: preparation refuses by name a fall whose foot the map gives a level as high as the lip's bed at any stage or gauge in the declared ranges, and prepares one whose lip stands above that level throughout them. Four falls are refused, each beside a twin that prepares. Three are drowned only at the top of a range, and the twin's range stops short of the lip: into a basin, at its highest stage; into the reach below, at the top of that reach's own range of level; and into a short reach below that drains to a lake, at the lake's highest stage, which backs the reach up to the lip. The fourth falls into a short reach that drains to a lake, and the map's level at its foot is as high as the lip only at a lake stage inside the lake's range and lies below the lip at the lake's lowest stage and at its highest; its twin has the same reach, lake and range and a lip that stands above the map's level at the foot at every stage, and prepares. The test shows the fourth fall's three levels at the foot, at the lowest stage, the drowning stage and the highest. Guard: CPU tests on small beds of the map's answers and of the four refusals with their twins, and one GPU test of the same points; only Metal shows that the map the shaders sample names the same body and depth down the rock.
items.check: cargo nextest run --locked --offline -p thrum-river-model --test it -E 'test(/^brink_receiver::/)' --no-tests=fail && cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --features thrum-render/creation-counters --test falls_gpu
items.ask: Does preparation decide a drowned fall for a sea, a basin and a reach alike by one comparison of the lip's bed with the highest level the map itself gives at the foot over the whole of the declared ranges, the stages and gauges between their ends included, and not by a rule written for one kind of receiver or by the levels at the ends of the ranges alone?

work_packages.name: With the stream in flood the waterfall reads as heavy falling water from the side and the bank, with no curtain and no strand that ends hard at the pool, drawn the way shipped games draw a heavy fall today
work_packages.quality_bar: A heavy waterfall as a high-end game shipped in 2020 or later draws one, Horizon Forbidden West's falls first: a mass of white falling water with depth to it from the side, glassy at the lip, grained with fine streaks and never draped like cloth, whose foot is buried in spray and white water and never shows where a strand ends. It has that game's spray at the foot and not its mist: nothing drifts off the fall or hangs in the air. The bar is the same in Chrome for the curtain and the strand ends. Its light in a gorge's shade and at dusk is judged in WP7.

items.statement: At the highest gauge the island's fall is drawn as the design's layered fall with spray at its foot, and not as the one sheet tuned again: falling water on more than one surface in depth, white water lit as foam, no end cut or thinned above the pool, and spray along the plunge line whose amount follows the fall's power. Where a segment's path meets the receiving water is found by one calculation, from the fall record and the level the water map has under the path, which the drawing and the plunge's sources share. Each reader makes it on the reading of the map its own time is. The foot of the drawn fall, which is the fade at the receiving level and the spray's origin, drop and amount, takes it at the display's time, from the stage and gauge the frame shows. The births and impulses take it at the committed tick, as WP6 built them. The motion written on a continuing clump takes the clump's place at the last presentation, from the plunge line as that presentation had it. Where two of these readings are the same the result may be used for both. The drawing has no second way of finding where the water lands and fixes no place or level on the stored path. Everything drawn is made from the fall record, the display's time and the plunge line. The fall steps no state of its own from one frame to the next, and keeps from the last presentation only what motion needs. It is drawn by ruling 7's pass with that pass's outputs. Below the profile's threshold of discharge for each metre of lip a fall is WP6's sheet alone. The log gives the island profile's threshold, stand-off, spray reach and amount of spray, with the reason for each.
items.ask: Is where the falling water meets the receiving water found by one calculation that the drawing and the births and impulses share, with no second way of finding it in the drawing and no place or level fixed on the stored path? Do the fade at the receiving level and the spray's origin, drop and amount take it from the water map at the display's time, and do the births and impulses take it from the map at the committed tick? Is a continuing clump's earlier place, for the motion written on it, worked out at the last presentation's time from the plunge line of that presentation? Is everything drawn for the fall at the highest gauge computed from the fall record, the display's time and the plunge line, with no state of the fall's own stepped between frames? Is it drawn by ruling 7's pass, before the water's gather? Does it differ from WP6's sheet in mechanism as the design selects, with more than one surface in depth and spray along the plunge line whose amount follows the fall's power, and not by new values for the one sheet? Does the log give the island profile's four values with a reason for each?

items.statement: At the highest gauge the island's fall reads as heavy falling water and not as a curtain. From beside it the falling water has depth, with nearer water passing over farther, and an uneven outline that changes as it falls, with no comb of tongues or ribbons. From in front it is a mass of white water grained with fine streaks, with no broad smooth fold or sheen down it as on draped cloth and no hem of ends hanging above the pool; nothing holds its place or shape through a sequence and nothing repeats at a regular spacing. It is whiter and fuller than at the middle gauge, and faster at the foot than at the lip. At the lip it is still a smooth tongue that shows the rock behind it. Raised from the middle gauge to the highest in one take, the fall thickens with no jump. At the lowest and middle gauges the fall still shows what WP6.4's review passed.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the fall at the gauge's highest, at noon, from 2 m and 5 m in front, from beside it, from behind it and from 60 m and 200 m off, with stills cropped at native size of the lip, the middle and the foot; one take from 5 m in front as the gauge rises from the middle to the highest; and sequences at the lowest and middle gauges from 5 m in front and from beside, set beside WP6.4's reviewed captures. 1. From beside, the falling water has depth: nearer water passes over farther water, and its outline is uneven and changes as it falls. It is not a flat sheet, and no comb of long tongues or ribbons hangs from it. 2. From 2 m and 5 m in front it is a mass of white water grained with fine streaks. No broad smooth fold with a sheen runs down it as on draped cloth. 3. From in front no scallop, ribbon or gap holds its place or shape through the sequence, nothing repeats at a regular spacing across the fall, and no hem of rounded or pointed ends hangs above the pool. 4. The fall is whiter and fuller than at the middle gauge. 5. Followed through a sequence, the water moves faster near the foot than near the lip. 6. At the lip it is a smooth tongue, and in the still of the lip the rock behind shows through it, as in WP6.4's reviewed still of the lip at this gauge. 7. From behind and from 60 m and 200 m it reads as the same fall, with no card, edge or separate layer showing. 8. As the gauge rises from the middle to the highest the fall thickens with no jump or swap that can be seen. 9. At the lowest and middle gauges the fall shows each point WP6.4's review passed.

items.statement: At the highest gauge the falling water meets the pool in white water and spray. No strand or sheet shows a cut, flat or pointed end above the boil or through it, and no hard line runs where the water lands, from the bank, along the foot of the cliff, from beside the fall or from above. Spray stands along the foot in front of where the water lands; it rises and falls back, no higher than about half the fall's height, and none drifts away or hangs in the air. No clump shows as a card or a disc, and with the camera still the spray does not sparkle or crawl. As the gauge falls from its highest to a dry lip the spray thins and is gone with the fall. The pool keeps the boil, the foam, the rings and the waterline on the rock that WP6.5's review passed.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the plunge pool at the gauge's highest, with the interaction windows on the pool, from its bank at 2 m, looking along the foot of the cliff, from beside the fall and from 15 m above, each holding the camera still for at least 3 s; one from the bank as the gauge falls from its highest to a dry lip; and stills cropped at native size where the falling water lands. 1. No strand or sheet shows a cut, flat or pointed end above the boil or through it. 2. No hard line runs along where the falling water meets the pool. 3. The white of the falling water runs into the white of the boil, with no dark gap or step between them. 4. Spray stands along the foot, in front of where the water lands in each view. Its clumps rise and fall back, none rises above about half the fall's height, and none drifts away from the fall or hangs in the air. 5. With the camera still, no clump of spray shows as a card or a disc with a hard edge, and no single pixels sparkle or crawl in it. 6. As the gauge falls to a dry lip the spray thins, and it is gone when the lip is dry. 7. The pool's boil, its foam streaks, its rings and its waterline on the rock are there as in WP6.5's reviewed captures.

items.statement: With the heavy fall in place, the frame and the pool receive what the design holds for any recipe. The frame cases run at the highest gauge on WP6's small fall, with a profile of the test's own, on the recipe the registry selects on the Mac and on the portable fallback where the two differ. Where the test reads: it takes its places from that recipe's own coverage in the submitted frame, near the lip, at the middle and at the foot, and at an opening in the fall where the frame has one, and takes none from a path fixed in the test. The places where spray is drawn are those the frame covers nearer the camera than the same frame drawn with the profile's amount of spray set to nothing. Depth: at each covered place the depth written is nearer than the scene behind it, and at a point within the distance of the fall record's paths that the recipe declares. At an opening the depth is the scene's, as in the same frame drawn without falls. The scene orders against the water as it is seen, which two test surfaces show. Water is never drawn in front of the depth it wrote: with an opaque test surface stood 0.05 m nearer the camera than the depth read at a covered place, the frame drawn shows the surface there, with the surface's depth written and the place outside the recipe's coverage. And an outer layer's depth is its own and not the core's: at a height where the test's profile stands the outer layers at least 0.2 m off the core, an opaque test surface is stood in front of the fall record's path by half that stand-off, placed from the path and the profile and from no depth read in a frame, and the frame drawn shows water over part of it, at places inside the surface's outline that the recipe covers with a depth nearer than the surface's. Motion is written from unjittered positions. On the falling water, read above the spray reach, it is faster low on the fall than near the lip. On the spray it is the clump's own: for a clump the frame shows apart from the others in two successive submitted frames, whose coverage rose at least 2 pixels between them, the mean motion written on its places equals the shift of its coverage, which the test measures from the two frames, within 1 pixel. Reactive coverage is written where the water is white. A pause holds the frame, and a capture shows it at the capture's time. The spray follows the receiving water, with the gauge held at its highest. Over settled water: the fixture's receiving pool is raised through its stage range, from 0 m to 0.33 m; spray is drawn at both levels, and the highest place it is drawn, taken over the same run of ticks at each level, a run as long as a clump's flight, rises by at least 0.11 m. Between two ticks: the pool is raised from 0 m to 0.33 m in one tick and a frame is presented halfway through that tick, which shows the pool at 0.165 m; the highest place spray is drawn in that frame is within 0.03 m of the highest in a frame of the same tick and time drawn over a pool held at 0.165 m. The sheet's own case, WP6's, stays as it is, on its own profile, which gives no heavy threshold and so draws the sheet alone. The pool, at the highest gauge over the same ticks: the plunge sources and impulse records the engine submits, each segment's place, footprint, births of foam and submerged air and impulse, are the same to the bit under three cameras, two that hold the foot of the fall in view from different places and one turned away from the fall, and under each of those recipes; and they are the ones recorded from the same fixture, gauge and ticks before this work package's first change to how the fall is drawn, which the test holds as test data: the same segments, each place within 0.01 mm and each amount within one part in a million. They follow the committed tick and not the frame's place within it: over the tick that raises the pool from 0 m to 0.33 m, a run that presents that tick's frame a quarter of the way through it and a run that presents it three quarters of the way through submit the same plunge sources and impulse records, to the bit. A scene whose profile does not name falls, or names them and gives no heavy threshold, compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before this work package. Guard: cases in WP6's two test files on their small fall, run in the package's one test binary with a GPU required; only Metal shows what a recipe's shaders write to the frame and how the scene's depth orders against it, and the sources are read as the engine submits them in those runs, because the camera and the recipe exist only in a drawn scene.
items.check: THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo nextest run --locked --offline -p water-scene --test it -E 'test(/^falls_gpu::/) | test(/^plunge_gpu::/)' --no-tests=fail
items.ask: Does the frame case run on each recipe that draws the fall at the highest gauge and take every place it reads from that recipe's own coverage in the frame it reads, with none fixed from the sheet's path? Does it stand its first test surface from the depth it read at each covered place, on each of those recipes, and tell that the surface shows from the frame drawn with it? Is its second test surface placed from the fall record's path and the profile's stand-off alone, and would a recipe that depth-tests or writes an outer layer at the core's depth fail it? Does it compare the spray's motion with a shift it measures from the spray's coverage in two frames, so that a clump that writes no motion, or the motion of the falling water behind it, fails? Does the case between two ticks compare the frame that shows the pool halfway up with a frame of the same tick and time over a pool held at that level, so that spray placed from the tick's level fails? Does the pool case present the frame of the rising tick at two places within the tick and compare what is submitted to the bit, so that sources placed from the level shown fail? Were the sources the pool case compares against recorded before this work package's first change to how the fall is drawn, and do two of its cameras hold the foot of the fall in view from different places?

items.statement: In Chrome at the highest gauge the fall is drawn as the layered fall with spray at its foot, by the Mac's recipe or by the lighter portable fallback that recipe names, and it clears the two cues there as on the Mac: from beside it the falling water has depth and an uneven outline, with no comb of tongues or ribbons, and from the pool's bank no strand or sheet shows a cut, flat or pointed end above the boil or through it and no hard line runs where the water lands. The fall draws from lip to pool, the water moves faster at the foot than at the lip, and the pool below it foams. Guard: the `fall-flood` case of the browser script.
items.inspect: Chrome T2 `realtime` sequences of the fall at the gauge's highest, at noon, from beside it and from the plunge pool's bank at 2 m looking along the foot of the cliff, with the interaction windows on the pool, and a still of each cropped at native size. 1. The receipts show submitted engine time advancing through each take. 2. From beside, the falling water has depth and an uneven outline that changes as it falls; it is not a flat sheet, and no comb of long tongues or ribbons hangs from it. 3. From the bank, no strand or sheet shows a cut, flat or pointed end above the boil or through it, and no hard line runs along where the falling water meets the pool. Only these two views are judged in Chrome. A difference from the Mac's takes that leaves points 2 and 3 true is recorded and does not decide the item.

items.statement: With the fall at the highest gauge filling a third of the view the paired cost record is taken again at 2560×1440, beside WP6's. Each tripwire it trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.

The ledger's `E1.rivers` row, the provenance file and the log are current. The ledger says the fall's look at the highest gauge was judged on the island's fall, names what draws it there on the Mac and in Chrome, says its light in shade is unjudged until WP7, and still says that falls of other heights are unjudged by eye. The log names each thing the design's heavy fall asks for that was not built.
items.ask: Does the ledger claim no more than this work package's items proved, with visuals and device apart, and say the heavy fall's light in shade is unjudged? Does the log name each thing the design's heavy fall asks for that was not built?

work_packages.name: A visitor raises the lake, sets the stream's flow and takes the day from dawn to night, and the rivers and the waterfall hold up in motion, in shade and from under water, on the Mac and in Chrome
work_packages.quality_bar: Rivers and a waterfall that pass in a shipped high-end game: Red Dead Redemption 2's streams and Horizon Forbidden West's falls, stable under reconstruction, lit only by the engine's sky, and of one piece with the lake and the sea they join.

items.statement: The river selection, the stream's flow and the flow bands are typed controls in the example on the Mac and in Chrome, saved in its parameter file. Moving the stream's flow or the lake's level rebuilds nothing and resets no wake or foam.

Under reconstruction the running water, its foam and the fall hold up in motion: no shimmer on the riffle, no ghost behind a streak of foam or a falling strand, no smear as the camera pans, and a clean reset on a cut and on a change of the selection.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences under TAAU on the Mac and in Chrome: a pan along the stream at 2 m, a still camera on the riffle and on the fall, a walk past the fall at 5 m, and a cut between two of them.

items.statement: Ruling 7's shadow is built. On a sheet, on foam and in the surface's Sun lobe, the direct Sun is multiplied by the scene's lent Sun visibility at the surface point: with half a fall in a wall's shadow, the shadowed half's direct Sun is under 2% of the lit half's, and its sky light is unchanged. A scene with no shadows draws as before.
items.check: THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo nextest run --locked --offline -p water-scene --test it -E 'test(/^river_shade_gpu::/)' --no-tests=fail
items.ask: Is the visibility read through the lent operation `WATERS` WP16 built, once for each direct-Sun term, with no shadow map sampled by the water itself?

items.statement: In a gorge's shadow at a low Sun the fall, its foam and the stream are lit by the sky alone and sit in the scene's light, and where the Sun reaches them they brighten along the shadow's own edge.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the fall and the stream below it with the Sun at 10° and 25°, the valley wall's shadow lying across them, from 5 m and from 60 m.

items.statement: In a calm, with the Sun up, the caustic field over the riffle is made from the flow bands: a net moves on the riffle's bed and none lies under the pool.

From dawn to night the rivers and the fall are lit only by the engine's sky: at the waterline their light joins the ground's, the white of foam and sheet follows the Sun's colour down to dusk, and at night nothing glows.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the stream, the fall and the river's mouth at dawn, noon, sunset and night, each whole and cropped at native size at a waterline and at the fall's foot.

items.statement: Ruling 7's light holds on the heavy fall WP11 built. At the highest gauge, on the recipe the registry selects on the Mac and on the portable fallback where the two differ, with half the fall in a wall's shadow the shadowed half's direct Sun is under 2% of the lit half's and its sky light is unchanged, on its layers and its spray as WP7.3 proves on the sheet. In a gorge's shadow at a low Sun the heavy fall, its spray and the white water at its foot are lit by the sky alone and sit in the scene's light, and where the Sun reaches them they brighten along the shadow's own edge. At sunset their white follows the Sun's colour, and at night nothing glows. Guard: a case at the highest gauge for each of those recipes in WP7.3's test file, on its small fall, each named from `heavy_fall`; the check selects them by that name, requires a GPU and fails if it selects none, because only Metal shows what a recipe's shaders do with the lent Sun visibility.

items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the fall at the gauge's highest: with the Sun at 10° and 25° and the valley wall's shadow lying across the fall, from 5 m and from 60 m, which are WP7.4's views; and at sunset and at night from 5 m; each whole and cropped at native size at the foot of the fall. 1. Where the shadow lies, the falling water, its spray and the white water at its foot show no direct Sun, right up to the shadow's edge: none of the Sun-coloured white the lit part has, and no Sun glint. 2. In the shadow they are still lit, by the sky: their detail holds, the white water takes the sky's colour, and they sit with the shaded rock and pool beside them. A smooth part of the fall that mirrors bright sky may be brighter than the foam beside it; that is the sky's reflection and no fault, and no order of brightness between the fall and the foam is judged. 3. Where the Sun reaches the fall it brightens, along the shadow's own edge. 4. At sunset the white of the fall and of its spray follows the Sun's colour. 5. At night nothing on the fall glows.
